verdict.rationale: Isaac documents its own tools for the configuration and first-motion steps, mostly in simulation: importing robots from URDF/MJCF/CAD, configuring robot and sensor models, controllers and motion generation, a first standalone control script, and adding your own robots. It also ships ROS 2 packages deployable on Jetson. Nothing shows hardware driver bring-up for a new physical robot, and nothing supports the hours-versus-weeks speed claim. Missing for 10: hardware driver integration or bring-up tooling for physical robots, evidence of time-to-first-motion, an end-to-end real-robot bring-up workflow, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can bring up a new robot — drivers, configuration, first motion — in hours rather than weeks

citations.quote: Import robots and scenes from URDF, MJCF, Onshape CAD, or USD.
You can then assemble simulation scenes by assigning materials, enabling physics, and configuring robot and sensor models.
Robot Simulation: Tools for moving robots, such as controllers, motion generation and kinematics solvers, and policy integration.
Write your first standalone script to control robots and environments.
The platform is also designed so that you can add your own robots!
